title: Vector endpoint tail-hunt: reservoir ingress shaping + kernel autotune for p99 reduction
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Goal: Reduce p99 latency for the embeddings (vector) endpoint by combining an ingress-side reservoir sampler/reshaper, micro-batch shaping, and a profile-guided kernel autotune pass. Background: Over the past quarter we've seen recurring p99 spikes on the vector endpoint under mixed-tenant workloads. Existing mitigations (size-aware batching and opportunistic prefetch) reduce median latency but leave a ~200ms tail for certain request-size mixes and tenant burst patterns. Scope: 1) Implement a lightweight reservoir-based ingress reshaper that smooths bursts by probabilistically holding/resequencing low-priority requests for short windows; 2) Add a microbatch shaping layer that packs small vectors into fixed-size microbatches with backoff heuristics (to avoid unbounded waiting); 3) Implement a kernel-autotune controller that selects between two low-level kernel paths (fast-path quantized vs conservative) based on short-term sequence-length and tokenization profiles, using on-device per-GPU profiles; 4) End-to-end telemetry and guardrails (per-tenant p50/p90/p99 histograms, request fingerprinting, and fallback rules). Acceptance criteria: - 30–40% reduction in p99 vs baseline for mixed workload test harness (stable across 3 runs) - No more than 5% regression in median throughput for the dedicated pools - Feature gated behind runtime flag and gradual rollout to a canary cohort (5% of traffic) - Clearability: the ingress reshaper can be drained within 2s on shutdown Tasks (high-level): - Design: define reservoir parameters (window, reservoir size, priority weighting) and microbatch shaping backoff policy - Implementation: ingress reshaper component + microbatch packer in the vector endpoint ingress path - Kernel autotune: collector for short-term perf histograms; simple decision logic + fallback - E2E tests: synthetic burst scenarios, mixed-tenant replay from production traces, perf regression suites - Telemetry: new metrics, dashboards, alert thresholds - Rollout plan: internal canary -> customer canary -> gradual ramp Risks and mitigations: - Risk: reshaper increases tail under pathological burst shapes; mitigation: conservative default reservoir size and a fast-forward drain path for high-priority/low-latency tenants. - Risk: kernel autotune misclassifies and regresses throughput; mitigation: autotune only on stable profiles and default to conservative kernel if uncertainty > 0.2. - Risk: observability gaps; mitigation: include a lightweight per-request fingerprint in trace logs for offline analysis Dependencies: - runtime-1.18 kernel hook for fast-path selection (DEPENDS ON ENG-541002) - telemetry pipeline PR (metrics schema) (DEPENDS ON ENG-501120) Rollout notes: Start with dedicated-dev cluster canary, collect 72h of p99/p95/p50 by tenant, iterate on reservoir parameters. If we hit regressions, decouple shaping from kernel autotune and revert autotune first. Long-term follow-ups: adaptive reservoir sizing per-tenant, ML-driven kernel selector, and integration with cost optimizer (Redwood Optimize) to surface cost vs latency tradeoffs.

2026-03-12 — Diego Ramirez: Canary run (5% traffic) results: p99 reduced from baseline 240ms -> 150ms for mixed-replay; median throughput unchanged. Two tenants showed +10% latency increase — investigating tenant-specific reservoir config. Moving ticket to In Progress for parameter tuning.
